videos.title: Unboxing the iPhone Duo Folio with Kickstand
videos.description:
The $129 iPhone Duo Folio with Kickstand is exactly as advertised on the box: a cover made of Apple’s TechWoven material that protects the front and back of the device and has a built-in kickstand that can prop it up at various angles. The kickstand really came in handy for FaceTime calls and watching Netflix in bed. However, this accessory provides no protection for the titanium sides.

videos.title: Unboxing the Apple iPhone Duo
videos.description: The iPhone Duo is Apple’s biggest change to the iPhone since… well, the original iPhone. Throughout the last 19 years, Apple has taken the iPhone in many directions from the humble 3.5-inch original introduced in 2007—larger, smaller, and thinner. An iPhone has remained the same touchscreen slab of colorful home screen icons, despite offering faster performance, longer battery life, and better cameras. The iPhone Duo is Apple’s first attempt to evolve its iconic device into something much more.

videos.title: First Look: Apple TV 4K
videos.description:
There’s finally a new Apple TV 4K, and It wants you to use Siri to find your lost remote.

The big changes for the Apple TV 4K are that it now runs on an A19 chip, first found in the iPhone 17. That chip enables a specially-built AV1 decoder, which the Cupertino, California tech giant promised should offer better streaming at a lower bandwidth. videos.title: First Look at Apple HomeView Smart Hub Device
videos.description:
Apple is finally taking smart homes seriously.

The $299 HomeView, launching on November 13, has a 7-inch Liquid Retina touchscreen and is powered by Siri AI. It supports major smart home protocols, including Matter and Thread, for the widest compatibility with existing smart home devices. There are two versions of the HomeView: one with a built-in speaker in its base that resembles an old iMac G4, and one without it for mounting to walls.
